item.title: Texas homeowners secure $1.9 million settlement and protections over nearby data centre project
item.description: Homeowners in Westlake, Texas, have come to an agreement concerning a proposed data centre that had sparked concerns. The settlement includes a financial contribution from developer PowerHouse earmarked for noise reduction and fire safety measures. Furthermore, the project will adhere to specific operational limits and environmental safeguards to alleviate resident anxieties. Though this venture promises to enhance Westlake's revenue significantly, community opinions remain split regarding the development.
item.dc:creator: TOI World Desk

item.title: In 1997, Princess Diana stayed at Cape Town’s Tarrystone Estate, now listed for R150 million
item.description: Tarrystone Estate in Cape Town, once the South African home of Princess Diana’s younger brother, Charles Spencer, is now on the market for R150 million. Diana stayed at the property during her March 1997 visit to South Africa, just months before her death. The cottage where she stayed has been preserved on the sprawling estate.
item.dc:creator: TOI Real Estate Desk

item.title: Pennsylvania landowner's 4540 acre forest protected from subdivision, preserving public recreation access
item.description: The Western Pennsylvania Conservancy has notably secured a vital conservation easement for a sprawling 4,540-acre forest in Pennsylvania. This landmark agreement ensures the land is preserved from any future development, safeguarding its natural elements. Since its establishment in 1932, the organization has protected over 300,000 acres, emphasizing critical wildlife habitats and advocating for sustainable forestry. This initiative highlights the critical role of conservation efforts in the region's ecological future.
item.dc:creator: TOI Science Desk

item.title: Cat Reunited With Family: Rescuers find Isaac alive; he hid in a kitchen cabinet
item.description: In a heartwarming turn of events, 13-year-old Zariah Coleman was joyously reunited with her beloved cat, Isaac, four days after a devastating building collapse that claimed eight lives. Amid the wreckage, rescue teams from various organizations banded together, ultimately finding Isaac snugly tucked away in a kitchen cabinet. Despite the chaos, the reunion brought a precious moment of happiness for Zariah and her mother.
item.dc:creator: TOI World Desk

item.title: Court lets New Hampshire homeowners pursue group trespass claim over chemical water pollution
item.description: A federal appeals court has permitted New Hampshire homeowners to advance a class-action trespass claim against Saint-Gobain. However, the court denied group treatment for negligence and failure-to-warn claims due to individual property assessments. Contamination of drinking water due to PFOA emissions from a manufacturing plant has been identified. The ruling acknowledged the homeowners' right to seek compensation while leaving individual claims to be determined later.
item.dc:creator: TOI World Desk

item.title: Virginia court settles family dispute over Smith Mountain Lake home and inherited ownership shares
item.description: A legal conflict concerning a Virginia lakeside property has escalated to the state's Court of Appeals. The court determined that Joan Cabaniss holds a 50% ownership share, while her late husband's children retain the remaining half through his will. Disputes over inheritance and property rights, including a contested quitclaim deed from one child, have been addressed.
item.dc:creator: TOI World Desk

item.title: Missouri couple win $47,500 after former sellers block property sale over a paid-off mortgage
item.description: In a challenging situation, a couple in Missouri struggled to sell their home when previous sellers refused to acknowledge a cleared mortgage. This conflict prompted a court's decision to award them $47,500 in damages after evidence confirmed the mortgage was paid off. The ruling also covered legal fees, underscoring the critical need for transparent financial protocols in real estate dealings.
item.dc:creator: TOI World Desk

item.title: Rare 1911 Denver Mint gold coin found in family safe-deposit box could fetch $500,000+
item.description: A remarkable discovery has surfaced—a $10 gold coin from 1911 that was hidden away in a family safe deposit box. Graded PCGS MS 65 and sanctioned by Certified Acceptance Corporation, this rare find is projected to sell for over $500,000 at an auction in January 2027. With only about 1,650 known examples in existence, such rare items often remain undetected until expert grading brings them into the spotlight.
item.dc:creator: TOI World Desk

item.title: Tom Holland and Zendaya buy £8.25 million London mansion at £750,000 discount
item.description: Tom Holland and Zendaya have reportedly purchased an £8.25 million mansion in London, paying £750,000 below its asking price. The five-bedroom property spans over 5,000 square feet and sits on an acre of land. The reported cash purchase adds another impressive real estate investment to the couple’s growing property portfolio.
item.dc:creator: TOI Real Estate Desk

item.title: Lady Gaga’s former NYC penthouse, also home to Carmelo Anthony, Tracy Morgan, listed for $7 million
item.description: Lady Gaga’s former New York City penthouse has hit the market for $6.995 million. The 3,700-square-foot luxury duplex, which was also once home to Carmelo Anthony and Tracy Morgan, features three bedrooms, a chef’s kitchen and a sprawling terrace offering stunning city views. The property is located in the iconic Hit Factory Condominium.

item.title: Missouri university employee keeps $631,000 discrimination award; retrial ordered
item.description: In a recent ruling, a Missouri court confirmed the jury's conclusion that Lincoln University established a racially hostile work setting for Sheila Gassner. The court did, however, nullify the damages linked to her constructive discharge claim and called for a new trial. Gassner, who endured heavy workloads while overseeing various departments, encountered discrimination after she raised issues.
item.dc:creator: TOI World Desk

item.title: Sergey Brin puts Malibu estate on the market for $33.5M
item.description: Sergey Brin and Nicole Shanahan have decided to sell their Malibu home for $33.5 million. After initially listing it as a luxury rental for $175,000, they opted to sell. The home includes five bedrooms and offers direct access to Little Dume Beach. Previously owned by pop singer Pink, the estate features impressive amenities and ocean views. Brin continues to invest in Malibu real estate, owning multiple properties in the area.

item.title: Bruce Springsteen's $50 million New Jersey archive opens, housing 48,000-plus items
item.description: Monmouth University in New Jersey has proudly unveiled the Bruce Springsteen Center for American Music, featuring over 48,000 artifacts that delve into the rich heritage of American music and celebrate the impact of Bruce Springsteen. Its inaugural exhibit highlights the evolution of protest music across history, and interactive setups invite attendees to immerse themselves in the experience.
item.dc:creator: TOI World Desk

item.title: Carrion crows can decide which way a cloud of dots was moving in about 235 milliseconds
item.description: In a fascinating study from the University of Tübingen, researchers discovered that carrion crows possess a remarkable ability to determine the direction of moving dots far more swiftly than both humans and monkeys. Their decision-making occurs in a mere 235 milliseconds, with neural activity indicating decision processes before physical actions take place. This research enhances our understanding of the rapid cognitive capabilities present in various animal species.
item.dc:creator: TOI Science Desk

item.title: Texas man loses $105,000 property claim after failing to trace inheritance in divorce case
item.description: A Texas appellate court has confirmed a lower court's decision regarding the divorce property division between Julian and Alice Devon Poole. Julian claimed certain assets as his separate property, including his inheritance and savings. However, the court found he failed to substantiate his claims adequately, leading to a ruling that mandates an equal division of marital assets between the spouses, thus upholding the trial court's verdict.
